<div class="hero-lead">From chromatin mechanisms to practical analysis; from experimental models to clinical inference. A navigable collection of free teaching material, built around what a dataset can—and cannot—establish.</div>

<div class="eyebrow">Four connected learning tracks</div>

## Follow the biological question, not only the technique

<p class="section-intro">Begin on a laptop, move to an HPC cluster, interrogate regulatory DNA and learn how to distinguish a promising cancer model from a clinically useful biomarker.</p>

```{=html}
<div class="track-grid">
<a class="track-card" href="tracks/computational.html"><div class="track-number">01 / COMPUTATIONAL</div><h3>Computational genomics</h3><p>Sequence data, reproducibility, local workflows, HPC, and high-dimensional analysis.</p></a>
<a class="track-card" href="tracks/experimental.html"><div class="track-number">02 / EXPERIMENTAL</div><h3>Experimental epigenomics</h3><p>Assay mechanisms, controls, quantitative interpretation and limitations.</p></a>
<a class="track-card" href="tracks/cancer.html"><div class="track-number">03 / CANCER BIOLOGY</div><h3>Cancer biology & models</h3><p>Enhancers, cell states, colorectal cancer organoids, and disease heterogeneity.</p></a>
<a class="track-card" href="tracks/translational.html"><div class="track-number">04 / TRANSLATIONAL</div><h3>Translational oncology</h3><p>Biomarker validation, study design, clinical endpoints, and useful evidence.</p></a>
</div>

```

## Begin with a challenging question

```{=html}
<div class="lesson-collection">
<a class="module-card" href="lessons/local-to-hpc.html"><span class="label">Computational · Foundations</span><h3>From laptop to HPC</h3><p>Inspect sequencing reads, document provenance, and understand scheduled computing.</p><span class="module-next">Read lesson →</span></a>
<a class="module-card" href="lessons/cutrun-benchmarking.html"><span class="label">Epigenomics · Intermediate</span><h3>When peak callers disagree</h3><p>Compare computational outputs without mistaking agreement for accuracy.</p><span class="module-next">Read lesson →</span></a>
<a class="module-card" href="lessons/hic-resolution-lab.html"><span class="label">3D Genomics · Interactive</span><h3>What survives Hi-C resolution?</h3><p>Change depth, binning and normalization in an original simulated contact map.</p><span class="module-next">Explore lesson →</span></a>
<a class="module-card" href="lessons/enhancer-to-organoid.html"><span class="label">Cancer biology · Advanced</span><h3>Is that enhancer causal?</h3><p>Assess accessibility, chromatin contacts, perturbation, and model context.</p><span class="module-next">Read lesson →</span></a>
<a class="module-card" href="lessons/hic-structures.html"><span class="label">3D Genomics · Illustrated</span><h3>How does the genome fold?</h3><p>Recognize compartments, contact domains, boundaries, loops and stripes—and distinguish maps from molecular mechanisms.</p><span class="module-next">Explore lesson →</span></a>
<a class="module-card" href="lessons/comparing-hic-samples.html"><span class="label">3D Genomics · Comparative analysis</span><h3>What changes between Hi-C samples?</h3><p>Compare two conditions, then multiple samples, while separating technical bias from candidate structural change.</p><span class="module-next">Explore lesson →</span></a>
<a class="module-card" href="lessons/hic-assays.html"><span class="label">Experimental · Methods selection</span><h3>Which 3D-genome assay fits your question?</h3><p>Compare targeted 3C methods, Hi-C and Micro-C, protein-enriched contacts, GAM and SPRITE.</p><span class="module-next">Explore lesson →</span></a>
<a class="module-card" href="lessons/atac-quality.html"><span class="label">Experimental · QC</span><h3>Can you trust your ATAC-seq library?</h3><p>Interpret TSS enrichment, FRiP, fragment lengths, mapping and replicates.</p><span class="module-next">Read lesson →</span></a>
<a class="module-card" href="lessons/chromatin-assays.html"><span class="label">Experimental · Methods</span><h3>ChIP, CUT&RUN or CUT&Tag?</h3><p>Biochemistry, controls, target context and appropriate inference.</p><span class="module-next">Read lesson →</span></a>
<a class="module-card" href="lessons/organoid-epigenomics-design.html"><span class="label">Organoids · Study design</span><h3>Design the biological unit</h3><p>Plan replicates and assay integration without mistaking cells for independent samples.</p><span class="module-next">Read lesson →</span></a>
<a class="module-card" href="lessons/gosling-genome-tracks.html"><span class="label">Interactive · Visualization</span><h3>Explore genomic evidence with Gosling</h3><p>Inspect BED, bedGraph and toy matrices, then try a public Gosling chart.</p><span class="module-next">Open studio →</span></a>
<a class="module-card" href="lessons/biomarker-evidence.html"><span class="label">Translational · Seminar</span><h3>Can an organoid result guide care?</h3><p>Critically appraise model-derived biomarkers with synthetic cases.</p><span class="module-next">Read lesson →</span></a>
</div>

```

## Built for scientifically grounded teaching

Primary literature, original explanatory figures, reproducible exercises and specific interpretation questions are embedded throughout. Toy examples are always identified as synthetic; the site is a developing resource and not evidence that each module has been delivered as a formal course.

[Teaching approach →](teaching.qmd)
:::
